The cloners. The Jedi. And even the Mandalorians. By aggregating the best of each, I will create an army that will bring order to the galaxy.|Gideon|}} '''Gideon's Imperial remnant''' was a [[Neo-Imperialism|neo-Imperialist]] [[Imperial Remnant|Imperial remnant]] part of the [[Neo-Imperial forces]] that continued their [[New Order|loyalty]] to the ousted [[Galactic Empire]] during the [[New Republic Era]] despite the Empire's [[Galactic Concordance|collapse]] after the [[Battle of Jakku]] at the end of the [[Galactic Civil War]]. Commanded by the [[warlord]] [[Moff]] [[Gideon]] [[Mandalore Imperial base|from]] [[Mandalore]], the well armed Imperial remnant hid in the [[Outer Rim Territories]] while attempting to bring about Gideon's vision of order to [[the galaxy]] and the completion of the [[Great Purge of Mandalore|purging]] of the [[Mandalorian]]s. Around the [[Standard year|year]] [[9 ABY]], Gideon's forces came into contact with [[Din Djarin]], a Mandalorian [[bounty hunter]] whom "[[the Client]]" hired on [[Nevarro]] to [[Mission to Arvala-7|retrieve]] an asset named [[Din Grogu|Grogu]]. Although the Mandalorian delivered Grogu to the remnant, he later had a change of [[heart]] and [[Incident on Nevarro|rescued]] Grogu. The remnant then occupied the local [[Nevarro City|town]] but was [[Clash on Nevarro|driven off]] when Djarin returned and defeated Moff Gideon, who returned his [[Gideon's fleet|fleet]]. The Moff continued his operations and used an army of third generation [[Dark Trooper]]s to assist him. Gideon managed to succeed in [[Battle of Tython (9 ABY)|capturing]] the child on [[Tython]], before [[Jedi Master]] [[Luke Skywalker]] [[Second rescue of Grogu|rescued]] him and defeated the Dark Troopers. Moff Gideon was arrested by the New Republic, and his key scientist [[Penn Pershing|Pershing]] defected to their [[New Republic Amnesty Program|amnesty program]], before Gideon managed to [[Extraction of Moff Gideon|escape]] and work in the shadows on the world of Mandalore. With an army of commandos at his disposal, alongside reinforcements provided by the [[Shadow Council]], Gideon's faction fought in one final [[Conflict on Mandalore|battle]] against the Mandalorians who sought to reclaim their homeworld, in which they ultimately met their defeat. ==Description== {{Quote|The Empire improves every system it touches. Judge by any metric. Safety, prosperity, trade, opportunity, peace.|"The Client"|}} [[File:Attempt_to_retake_Mandalore_MandoS3.png|thumb|left|300px|The Galactic Empire splintered into various Imperial Remnants, one of which was led by Moff Gideon.]] Having attained the [[Military rank|rank]] of [[moff]],{{TheMandalorian|Chapter 8: Redemption}} Gideon led a sizable remnant{{Topps|set=2022 Topps Finest Star Wars|cardname=Moff Gideon}} of Imperial forces and united remnants as a [[warlord]]. Moff Gideon was an imposing and ruthless leader, and also a patriot of the [[Galactic Empire]] who was known to kill fellow Imperials should they endanger his cause. Gideon forces inherited assets from the [[Imperial Military]], specifically from the [[Imperial Army]] and [[Imperial Navy]] and used them as a well established military force to achieve its objectives. Remnant forces on [[Nevarro]] had the capability to occupy and maintain order on the planet and maintained at least [[Gideon's battalion|one battalion]]. The remnant's frontline [[infantry]] were comprised of [[stormtrooper]]s, [[Imperial armored commando]]s, [[scout trooper]]s, at least one [[Incinerator stormtrooper|incinerator trooper]] and one [[artillery stormtrooper]]. Local stormtroopers on Nevarro were of lower class and quality, merely serving as [[bodyguard]]s for important high ranking Imperial officials or to maintain the occupation of [[Nevarro City]]. Additionally, the remnant led by Moff Gideon utilized elite [[death trooper]]s on Nevarro, which formed a [[Gideon's guard|guard unit]] protecting Gideon, as well as a [[Gideon's Dark Trooper platoon|platoon]] of [[Phase-III Dark Trooper]]s and later utilised the new [[Dark Trooper phase 4]] armor which was used by Gideon himself. Three [[Praetorian Guard|Imperial Praetorian Guards]] were later used to act as a bodyguard for Gideon{{TheMandalorian|Chapter 12: The Siege}} [[Imperial officer]]s also served within the remnant, serving in various capacities including [[captain]]ing a [[starship]], acting as [[security officer]]s, [[deck officer]]s, [[pilot]]s, [[communications officer]]s and [[gunnery officer]]s. The remnant also consisted of [[scientist]]s including [[Cloning|clone]] [[Bioengineering|engineers]] and Imperial Department of Military Research scientists. [[File:Troopers-Guarding-City-The-Mandalorian.png|thumb|right|250px|Gideon's forces were active on Nevarro.]] Weapons used by the remnant included the typical [[E-11 medium blaster rifle]], [[SE-14r light repeating blaster]], [[E-22 reciprocating double-barreled blaster rifle]], or the [[DLT-19 heavy blaster rifle]]. Scout troopers used the [[EC-17 hold-out blaster]], and death troopers used the [[E-11D blaster carbine]]. They also used [[E-HOB heavy repeating laser cannon|E-Web heavy repeating blaster cannons]]. Furthermore, Imperial forces were bolstered by [[armor]]ed units including a [[K79-S80 Imperial Troop Transport]], [[74-Z speeder bike]]s, a [[Trexler 906 Armored Marauder]], and other vehicles. Their leader, Moff Gideon, also used a personal [[Outland TIE fighter]], a model of the [[Sienar Fleet Systems]]' [[TIE series|TIE fighter series]],{{SWCT|set=Star Wars: The Mandalorian - Illustrated Outlaws|cardname=Outland TIE Fighter}} with wings that folded when landing on a leveled surface, allowing for ease of access to the cockpit. They also owned at least two [[RA-7 protocol droid]]s, [[Unidentified RA-7 protocol droid bartender|one]] of whom served the Nevarro cantina as the [[bartender]] after the remnant's occupation of the [[planet]], while another served on Gideon's [[cruiser]], as well as [[R-series]] astromech droids, [[Power droid]]s, including at least one [[MPH power droid]], [[MSE-6 series repair droid]]s and at least [[Unidentified probe droid (Gideon)|one]] [[Viper probe droid]]{{TheMandalorian|Chapter 16: The Rescue}} A [[Gideon's fleet|fleet]] also served under Moff Gideon's command, as part of his Imperial remnant. The fleet included a modified [[Gozanti-class Assault Carrier|''Gozanti''-class Assault Carrier]], a [[Class 546 Cruiser|Class 546]] [[Gideon's light cruiser|light cruiser]], several Outland TIE fighters, [[TIE/ln space superiority starfighter]]s, a [[Gideon's TIE/IN interceptor squadron|squadron]] of [[TIE/IN interceptor]]s,{{TheMandalorian|Chapter 19: The Convert}} a [[Gideon's TIE/sa bomber squadron|squadron]]{{InsiderCite|222|Star Wars: The Mandalorian Season Three Companion|''Star Wars: The Mandalorian'' Season Three Companion}} of [[TIE/sa tactical bomber|TIE/sa bombers]], several [[Imperial Troop Transport|Imperial transports]] and [[Shuttle 2743|one]] [[Lambda-class T-4a shuttle|''Lambda''-class T-4a shuttle]]. ==History== ===Origins=== {{Quote|Moff Gideon was executed for war crimes.''"
"''It's him.|Carasynthia Dune and Din Djarin|}} For a [[Imperial Era|period]] of [[time]] following the [[Clone Wars|end]]{{Film|III}} of the [[Galactic Republic]], the [[Galactic Empire]] reigned over [[the galaxy]], enforcing [[Galactic Emperor|Emperor]] [[Darth Sidious|Sheev Palpatine's]][[Tarkin (novel)|''Tarkin'']] rule with an [[iron]] fist through a massive technological [[Imperial Military|military force]].{{Databank|galactic-empire|Galactic Empire}} However, the [[Alliance to Restore the Republic]] rebelled in the [[Galactic Civil War]] and achieved a series of decisive victories,{{Film|IV}} culminating at the [[Battle of Endor]] in [[4 ABY]],''[[Star Wars: Galactic Atlas]]'' where the Emperor was [[Death|killed]] alongside his chief enforcer, [[Anakin Skywalker|Darth Vader]], and the [[DS-2 Death Star II Mobile Battle Station|second]] planet-[[Superweapon|destroying]] [[Death Star]] [[battle station]] was destroyed.{{Film|VI}} Without a [[Darth Sidious|leader]] to keep the Empire united, the remnants of the Empire began to fracture''[[Star Wars: The Force Awakens: The Visual Dictionary]]''[[Aftermath (novel)|''Aftermath'']] into Imperial holdouts.{{TheMandalorian|Chapter 10: The Passenger}} [[File:VillainsVader-ImperialArmy.png|thumb|left|300px|The Galactic Empire once dominated the galaxy in part through its technological war machine.]] However, across [[Realspace|space]], Imperial [[Moff]]s and regional [[governor]]s still had control over their [[sector]]s, [[star system]]s, and planets,''[[Aftermath: Life Debt]]'' while Imperial [[fleet]]s and [[Army|armies]] remained scattered across the [[galaxy]]. In wake of the chaos after [[Endor]],{{Databank|rae-sloane|Rae Sloane}} Moffs and regional governors began vying for power and jockeying against each other for position and control in the power vacuum left behind by Emperor Palpatine's death.{{Marvel|subdomain=comicstore|url=Journey-to-Star-Wars-The-Force-Awakens-Shattered-Empire/comics-series/51939|text=Journey to Star Wars: The Force Awakens - Shattered Empire}} The Imperial Military was unable to be reined in, with different warlords and remnants grabbing at power.''[[Star Wars: Squadrons]]'' After the [[Battle of Jakku]], the Imperial armed forces were totally shattered, and the Empire formally [[Imperial Instruments of Surrender|surrendered]] to the [[New Republic]],''[[Aftermath: Empire's End]]'' the government established by the Rebel Alliance.''[[Lost Stars]]'' The weakened Empire signed a truce and [[Galactic Concordance|peace treaty]] with the emboldened New Republic, ending the Galactic Civil War and dissolving the Galactic Empire. Nevertheless, remnants of the Empire continued to persist in the form of Imperial holdouts, fragments of the former [[New Order|regime]] which gained footholds on distant worlds,{{Databank|stormtroopers|Stormtroopers}} after the Empire's collapse. Former Imperials became [[warlord]]s while remnant [[stormtrooper]]s dissolved into [[mercenary]] bands in service to the ex-Imperial warlords.{{TheMandalorian|Chapter 3: The Sin}} One such Imperial remnant was led by Moff [[Gideon]], a former [[officer]] in the [[Imperial Security Bureau]] during the [[Mandalorian]] [[Great Purge of Mandalore]], who formed his faction out of the remains of the [[Imperial Army]]{{SWCT|set=2021 Base|cardname=Moff Gideon}} and [[Imperial Navy]] to achieve his ends in a campaign to return Imperial order to the galaxy. ===Operations on Nevarro=== ====Ongoing Experiments==== {{Quote|Compare Imperial rule to what is happening now… Look outside. Is the world more peaceful since the revolution? I see nothing but death and chaos.|"The Client," to Din Djarin|}} [[File:The_Client_and_stormtroopers.png|thumb|right|270px|Din Djarin's client was a follower of Moff Gideon, who sought to acquire a Force-sensitive child.]] By [[9 ABY]],{{MandoDate}} during the [[New Republic Era]], Moff Gideon's Imperial remnant operated nearby and had clandestinely established operations on the [[Outer Rim Territories|Outer Rim]] planet''[[The Star Wars Book]]'' [[Nevarro]], including a [[Imperial Remnant safe house|facility]] in the local [[Nevarro City|town]]{{TheMandalorian|Chapter 1: The Mandalorian}} and a restarted [[Nevarro Imperial base|Imperial base]] on another side of the planet. Gideon further commanded a [[Gideon's fleet|fleet]] and Imperial [[scientist]]s and [[engineer]]s like [[Doctor]] [[Penn Pershing]]. On Nevarro, Gideon used an ex-Imperial, "[[the Client]]," and his stormtrooper guard as fronts for his operation. The [[Bounty Hunters' Guild]] also maintained a presence on Nevarro, where former [[magistrate]] [[Greef Karga]] acted as an expeditor for the guild, running the [[Bounty hunter|bounty hunting]] trade{{Databank|greef-karga|Greef Karga}} in the [[Dalicron sector|sector]] from Nevarro. As part of a series of ongoing experiments involving [[blood]] transfusions overseen by Doctor Pershing, Gideon and his forces sought to [[Hunt for Grogu|acquire]] a mysterious{{Databank|grogu|Grogu}} [[Force-sensitive]]{{TheMandalorian|Chapter 2: The Child}} [[alien]] [[youngling]] known as [[Din Grogu|Grogu]]. Gideon used the force of the remains of the [[Imperial Army]] to acquire it. In 9 ABY, the Client hired a Mandalorian [[bounty hunter]] named [[Din Djarin]], having been sent by Karga, to [[Mission to Arvala-7|locate and acquire]] a highly valuable "asset" on [[Arvala-7]]. In return, the Client offered Djarin a substantial reward in the form of [[beskar]], a [[metal]] alloy''[[Star Wars Rebels: Heroes of Mandalore]]'' traditionally used to forge ancestral [[Mandalorian armor]] which the Empire had stolen from [[Mandalore]] as spoils of the Purge. Aside from the age of the asset, which was approximately fifty [[Standard year|years]] old, the Client offered little else to help the Mandalorian. Nevertheless, he was confident that such a highly skilled and expensive [[Soldier|warrior]] would complete the task. After returning from Arvala-7, the Mandalorian fulfilled his [[Bounty|commission]] by handing over the asset, which he had discovered to be Grogu, to the Client and Dr. Pershing. Once the Mandalorian was gone, the Client and Pershing argued about the infant, with the Client demanding he simply remove the material that they needed from Grogu even if the procedure resulted in his [[death]]. Pershing refused, reminding the Client that they had orders to deliver him alive, after which the Client warned Pershing that his safety was no longer assured. Soon after, the Mandalorian returned to [[Incident on Nevarro|rescue]] Grogu, having had a change of heart, resulting in a firefight with the remnant stormtroopers. Though outnumbered, the Mandalorian defeated the [[trooper]]s and ultimately escaped from the facility with Grogu ====Gideon's arrival==== {{Quote|You have something I want. You may think you have some idea of what you are in possession of, but you do not. In a few moments, it will be mine. It means more to me than you will ever know.|Gideon, to Din Djarin|}} [[File:GideonRemnant-TMS01E07.jpg|thumb|left|300px|Gideon and his forces confronted the Mandalorian bounty hunter who became Grogu's guardian.]] Following the theft of Grogu, the Client and his forces installed a renewed Imperial authority across the city on Nevarro. A number of bounty hunters tried and failed to recapture the Child,{{TheMandalorian|Chapter 4: Sanctuary}}{{TheMandalorian|Chapter 5: The Gunslinger}} and so a plan was put in place for Karga to lure Djarin back to the planet to kill him in order to free Nevarro from the Imperial presence. However, after Grogu [[Force healing|saved]] Karga's life, Karga killed his accompanying bounty hunters and sided with the Mandalorian and his allies, [[Carasynthia Dune|Cara Dune]] and [[Kuiil]]. Planning to kill the Client instead, Karga and Dune escorted a handcuffed Djarin through the city with a decoy of Grogu, eventually reaching the [[Nevarro school|cantina]]. Upon arriving, the Client expressed his admiration of the Mandalorian's new armor and questioned him as to why [[Mandalore]] had resisted Imperial expansion, claiming that the Empire improved every system it touched. Their discussion was interrupted when the Client was contacted by Moff Gideon via [[hologram]], who then ordered a [[squad]] of [[death trooper]]s outside to fire on the [[cantina]], killing the Client and his stormtrooper guards. Gideon then flew down beside the cantina in an [[Outland TIE fighter]], backed by his [[Gideon's guard|death trooper guard]] and the rest of his [[Gideon's battalion|stormtrooper battalion]]. Meanwhile, [[scout trooper]]s were able to track down and retake Grogu, killing his guardian, Kuiil. ====Clash on Nevarro==== {{Quote|If you're asking if you can trust me, you cannot. Just as you betrayed our business arrangement, I would gladly break any promise and watch you die at my hand. The assurance I give is this: I will act in my own self-interest, which at this time involves your cooperation and benefit.|Gideon, stating terms of surrender to Greef Karga|}} At the cantina, Gideon began talking across to the Djarin, Karga and Dune from outside, emphasizing Grogu's importance to him. He gave the three until nightfall to surrender, threatening to use an [[E-HOB heavy repeating laser cannon|E-Web heavy repeating blaster cannon]] on them if they failed to do so. At the same time, the scout troopers who had acquired Grogu rendezvoused near the city. They listened in on transmissions as Gideon killed one of his officers out of anger. The pair were suddenly approached by the bounty hunter [[droid]] [[IG-11]], which Kuiil had reprogrammed for nursing and protection. In the ensuing confrontation, the droid neutralized both scout troopers and then took Grogu with him on one of their [[74-Z speeder bike]]s. [[File:NevarroBattle.png|thumb|right|250px|Gideon's stormtroopers were decimated by IG-11, an assassin-turned-nurse droid.]] IG-11 rode into Nevarro city on the seized [[speeder bike]], carrying Grogu in a bag hanging over his front and shooting nearby stormtroopers he passed. When the droid reached the clearing next to the cantina where Djarin and his comrades were pinned down, IG-11 jumped off of the speeder bike, allowing it to crash into the stormtroopers and Death troopers ahead. As IG-11 proceeded to [[Clash on Nevarro|fight]] his many adversaries, Djarin, Dune and Karga joined the battle, killing many troopers in the firefight. As Djarin used the E-Web blaster cannon to mow down more stormtroopers, Gideon arrived, and shot an explosive object near the Mandalorian, injuring him. Subsequently, IG-11 and the rest of Djarin's comrades helped him back inside the cantina under fire. Gideon ordered an [[Incinerator stormtrooper|incinerator trooper]] to burn the cantina with Djarin and the others inside. However, Grogu used [[the Force]] to turn the fire back to the trooper, killing him. Djarin's group then retreated into the sewers and visited a [[Nevarro Mandalorian covert|covert]]. By the time stormtroopers arrived at the enclave, Djarin and his comrades had left, leaving [[the Armorer]], who fought and defeated the troopers. Another group of stormtroopers awaited Djarin's group at the end of a tunnel. IG-11, though, [[Self-destruct mechanism|self-destructed]] to defeat the [[squad]]. As the rest of the group left the tunnel, they were attacked by Gideon in [[Gideon's Outland TIE fighter|his]] [[Outland TIE fighter]]. Djarin chased the TIE with his [[jetpack]] and planted a [[detonator]] on it, damaging it and causing it to crash. With Gideon defeated, Djarin parted ways with Dune and Karga and departed Nevarro with Grogu. ===Hunting the Child=== ====Skirmish on Trask==== {{Quote|We need to hold them off until we can make a jump to hyperspace.|The deck officer, to his stormtroopers|}} [[File:Mando_chap_11_gozanti.png|thumb|left|260px|A group of Mandalorians targeted a ''Gozanti''-class cruiser belonging to Moff Gideon.]] After successfully helping a [[Frog Lady|passenger]] and her eggs reach [[Trask]] and reunite with her [[Frog Man|husband]], Djarin was recruited by [[Bo-Katan Kryze]], [[Koska Reeves]], and [[Axe Woves]] to help them raid a [[Gozanti-class Assault Carrier|''Gozanti''-class Assault Carrier]] belonging to the remnant in order to capture some weapons being exported from the [[black market]] port. The quartet of [[Mandalorian]]s fought through several units of [[stormtrooper]]s to reach the cargo hold. The quartet were temporarily stopped by a remnant officer who trapped them in the cargo control area. The officer and a group of stormtroopers that accompanied him in defending the hold were jettisoned. After Kryze revealed to the [[Unidentified Imperial captain|captain]] that he had captured the cargo hold, the captain stated that even if they jettisoned the crates of cargo, they would comb the area and kill them. Kryze revealed that her true objective was to fully capture the ship and storm the [[Bridge (starship)|bridge]] even to the distraught and shock of Djarin. Djarin eventually agreed to help Kryze storm the bridge and fully capture the ship, in return Kryze would reveal the whereabouts of a [[Ahsoka Tano|Jedi]]. The captain contacted Gideon informing him of [[pirate]]s who previously raided their past shipments, he informed him of the loss of the cargo hold and requested reinforcements. This only prompted Gideon to order the captain to scuttle the ship via the phrase "Long live the Empire," he proceeded to kill his own bridge personnel and personally piloted the ship to scuttle into the [[ocean]] of Trask. [[File:NiteOwlsGozanti.png|thumb|right|250px|The Mandalorians captured the cruiser, killing the Imperial personnel aboard.]] With the Gozanti on a crash course with the ocean, the quartet of Mandalorians were slowed down by the suppressive fire of stormtroopers armed with [[DLT-19 heavy blaster rifle|heavy repeating blasters]] with the altitude of the ship dropping, Djarin drew two [[grenade]]s and ran at the stormtroopers while being covered by the others. After heavy fire and falling to the group, Djarin hurled the two grenades at the stormtroopers killing them. Upon reaching the bridge, Djarin and Reeves piloted the ship away from the ocean while Kryze interrogated the captain, asking if Gideon had the [[Darksaber]]. The captain informed her that she should already have known of this by asking the question. Kryze threatened to keep him alive but the captain simply stated that while she would let him live, Gideon would not. He took his own life via a [[Electro capsule|suicide shocker]], which killed him instantly. After Kryze revealed the location of the Jedi at the city of [[Calodan]] on the forest planet [[Corvus]]. Djarin and the Mandalorians parted ways, with Kryze, Reeves, and Woves maintaining control of the captured cruiser. ====Capturing the Child==== {{Quote|Does he still have the asset?''"
"''Yes. Our source confirmed it.''"
"''And we will be ready.|Gideon and Elia Kane|}} At one point, Gideon received a hologram message from Dr. Pershing, who was apologizing to him for failing an experiment involving the Child and [[Strand-Cast]]s. He also reported that he had exhausted their supply of Grogu's blood samples, and that he required more genetic material from the donor in order to continue his work.{{TheMandalorian|Chapter 12: The Siege}} Three days later, Djarin went back to Nevarro in need of repairs and was recruited by Karga, Dune, and a [[The Fledgling Mythrol|Mythrol]] to join them on their own mission to destroy the Imperial base. As the four undertook the mission, a [[Mimbanese|Mimbanesse]] [[Unidentified Mimbanese worker|worker]] and placed a [[Homing beacon|tracking device]] on Djarin's ship. At the base, Djarin and the others viewed the hologram of Pershing and realized that the Imperials were performing experiments, hence their pursuit of Grogu. The worker later contacted a [[Elia Kane|comms officer]] on [[Gideon's light cruiser]] informing her that the tracking device had been planted. The officer subsequently informed Gideon, who smiled to himself and continued to supervise the work of his scientists on his [[Phase-III Dark Trooper|Dark Troopers]]. [[File:The-Mandalorian-dark-troopers.png|thumb|left|250px|Gideon's Dark Troopers captured Grogu from Din Djarin on Tython.]] Gideon's forces tracked Djarin's ship to [[Tython]]. From high atmosphere, two [[Imperial Troop Transport|Imperial transports]] carrying a [[Tython detachment|detachment of stormtroopers]] launched from Gideon's [[light cruiser]]. As the stormtroopers did [[Battle of Tython (9 ABY)|battle]] with Djarin and his allies, [[Boba Fett]] and [[Fennec Shand]], four Dark Troopers were readied and launched from the cruiser and landed near the [[seeing stone]] where Grogu had been meditating. There, one of the Dark Troopers seized Grogu and flew upwards back to the cruiser with the other three Dark Troopers while Fett pursued them from his [[Slave I|ship]]. Upon seeing the cruiser, Fett remarked in disbelief that the Empire was back. Once the Dark Troopers returned to the cruiser with the Child, Gideon's cruiser jumped to [[hyperspace]], though not before blasting Djarin's grounded ship, the ''Razor Crest'', destroying it. While still in hyperspace, Gideon briefly talked to the Child in his prison cell, walking in on the child attacking two stormtroopers. Letting Grogu tire himself out battling the two troopers, Gideon showed Grogu the Darksaber before having his stormtroopers stun him and place him in shackles. Gideon then ordered his communications officer to send an encrypted message to Pershing, informing him that they had their donor for his experiments once they exited hyperspace. ====Attack on Gideon's cruiser==== [[File:DjarinDeliversGideon-TMCh16.png|thumb|right|250px|Djarin and his allies attacked Moff Gideon's cruiser, capturing him in the process.]] Djarin and his team [[Second rescue of Grogu|infiltrated]] Gideon's cruiser, and they split, Kryze searching for Gideon, and Djarin searching for the child. Gideon was prepared, and tried to trick the Mandalorian to lower his guard with promises of returning the Child, claiming to no longer need him, having already taken his blood. He attempted to strike at Djarin from behind, and proceeded to battle the Mandalorian, who fought back with his [[beskar spear]]. Gideon was defeated, and Djarin brought him to Kryze, and tried to return the Darksaber to her. Gideon laughed, knowing that she could not take the saber without winning it through combat. Then the dark troopers, which Djarin had ejected into space, returned via their [[rocket booster]]s. Confident that everyone besides himself will be killed by the Dark Troopers, he did not anticipate the arrival of [[Jedi Knight]] [[Luke Skywalker]]. After watching the [[Jedi]] destroy the Dark Troopers, Gideon tried to eliminate the child, and then kill himself. He failed to do both and was knocked unconscious so that [[Marshal]] Dune could use his invaluable ISB information for the New Republic and properly bring him to justice. Djarin believed that was very likely that the Moff would be executed for his crimes by the [[New Republic Tribunal]].{{BOBF|Chapter 5: Return of the Mandalorian}} ====Extracting Moff Gideon==== Following the [[Second rescue of Grogu|rescue of Grogu]] from Gideon's light cruiser, Gideon's communications officer, [[Elia Kane]] became part of the [[New Republic]]'s [[New Republic Amnesty Program|amnesty program]]. In truth, she had remained loyal to the Remnant and was acting as a spy for it. Sometime after his arrest by the New Republic, Gideon escaped New Republic custody when his [[beskar]]-plated [[Imperial armored commando|commandos]] [[Extraction of Moff Gideon|extracted]] him from the [[Lambda-class T-4a shuttle]] carrying him to his trial. After his escape he and his forces regrouped at their headquarters on Mandalore. ===Rulers of Mandalore=== ====From the shadows==== Having succeeded in acquiring Grogu's blood Gideon used it to create [[Gideon's clones|Force-sensitive clones]] of himself to incorporate into his army, as well as designing the [[Dark Trooper phase 4]] armor, which he wore to battle himself. To defend the [[Mandalore system]] the remnant used a large [[Gideon's TIE/IN interceptor squadron|squadron]] of [[TIE/IN interceptor]]s backed by [[TIE/sa tactical bomber|TIE/sa bombers]] and [[TIE/ln space superiority starfighter]]s. One of Gideon's subordinates Elia Kane was routinely used as the remnants contact with the larger galaxy. Gideon also hired [[Pirate King]] [[Gorian Shard]] and his [[Gorian Shard's pirate crew|pirate gang]] to cause chaos in the outer rim without alerting the New Republic specifically in [[Dalicron sector|Nevarro's sector]]. Several TIE interceptors and bombers were dispatched to destroy [[Kryze Fortress|Kryze Castle]] on [[Kalevala]] after Bo-Katan Kryze returned home. Worried that his former scientist Penn Pershing, who had also joined the New Republic's amnesty program, would reveal the secrets of his project to the wider galaxy, Gideon sent Elia Kane to erase his memory. Kane succeeded in framing Pershing of being a criminal, whilst simultaneously working her way up through New Republic ranks. As revenge for being driven off Nevarro, Gideon later sent [[Gorian Shard]]'s [[Gorian Shard's pirate crew|pirates]] to devastate the planet. However, their efforts were stopped by Mandalorians led by Djarin and Kryze. Kane learnt of this and informed Gideon that both Djarin's [[The Tribe|tribe]] and Kryze's [[Bo-Katan Kryze's unit|unit]] had joined together in defeating the pirates on Nevaro despite their animosity towards each other, to which he assured her that he would take care of the Mandalorians ====Meeting with the Shadow Council==== Afterwards Gideon attended a meeting with the [[Shadow Council (Imperial Remnants)|Shadow Council]]. He remained silent as he listened to the other members discussion. Irked by Captain [[Gilad Pellaeon]]'s zealous commitment to Grand Admiral Thrawn, Moff Gideon mockingly remarked on the [[Chiss]] commander's recurring absence and expressed doubt at his "imminent return". Pivoting from this point, he further stressed the need for new leadership, hinting at his own ambitions to take the reins. [[Commandant]] [[Brendol Hux]] instead suggested that [[Project Necromancer]] would solve that matter, before questioning Moff Gideon on Doctor Pershing's situation. The warlord denied using the scientist for his own experiments and changed the subject to the Mandalorian threat. Hux and Pellaeon agreed to grant Gideon extra resources as well as three [[Praetorian Guard|Imperial Praetorian Guards]] to protect him for the upcoming battle. With his request granted, the Moff ended the meeting with a [[Long live the Empire|patriotic chant]], joined in unison by his fellow warlords. ====Battle for Mandalore==== =====The trap===== [[File:GideonArmorCropped-SWI221.png|thumb|left|200px|Gideon revealed himself to the gathered forces of Mandalore in his new armor.]] When the Mandalorians under Kryze and Djarin returned and made their way to the [[Great Forge]], Gideon sent his commandos to lead them into a trap. As Kryze, Djarin, and their forces pursued the Imperials, they found themselves in Gideon's base. Djarin was then separated from the main group and taken prisoner by the commandos and Gideon, who had donned his beskar-derived fourth generation Dark Trooper armor. As Djarin was taken away, Gideon thanked him for bringing all the Mandalorians back to one place and sent his interceptors and bombers to deal with the [[Mandalorian fleet]]. Gideon demanded the Darksaber from Kryze, remembering how she gave to him when he offered a ceasefire before the Great Purge. Kryze, knowing too well, refused and cut through the blast doors to help her unit escape. [[Heavy Infantry Mandalorian]] [[Paz Vizsla]], despite Kryze's plea, made a last stand to cover their retreat; a number of commandos attempted and failed to take down the heavy fighter, necessitating the arrival of all three Praetorian Guards, who quickly felled and killed their opponent. =====Fall of the remnant===== Djarin managed to escape Imperial custody with help from Grogu. Together they infiltrated the base along with Grogu hoping to locate the command center and take Moff Gideon out once and for all. With assistance from [[R5-D4]] they managed to locate the command center. As they approached the command center they discovered Moff Gideon's Force-sensitive clones and destroyed them, thus ruining Gideon's plans to conquer the Galaxy. This prompted an enraged Gideon to attack Djarin on a platform near the command center when the two arrived there. While fighting with Gideon, the Praetorian Guards emerged and attacked Djarin, however Grogu stopped them causing the guards to charge at him who retreated back into the command center. After the Mandalorians regrouped, they launched an attack on Gideon's base with reinforcements from the fleet. Woves decided to remain on the light cruiser to act as a distraction for Gideon's interceptors and bombers.{{TheMandalorian|Chapter 24: The Return}} The Mandalorians used their [[Kom'rk-class fighter/transport|''Kom'rk''-class fighter transports]] to deploy an attack force. Using their jetpacks, the Mandalorians flew into the skytop opening, engaging Gideon's commandos, especially Kryze who used the Darksaber to eliminate several of them. After spotting Djarin fighting Gideon, Kryze then landed and fought with Gideon, allowing Djarin to leave and save Grogu. Using Grogu's force powers and Djarin's weapons, the pair managed to defeat all three Praetorian Guards. Gideon crushed the Darksaber with his suit's augmented strength, breaking Kryze's hand in the process and taunting her that without their toys, Mandalorians were weak. As Djarin and Grogu arrived, Kryze declared Mandalorians were stronger together, and the three quickly overpowered him. [[File:GideonFlameOn-MandoS3-Ch24.png|thumb|250px|The death of Moff Gideon marked the end of his remnant.]] With the light cruiser severely damaged, Woves steered it into the base and escaped at the last minute, before the cruiser crashed into the base destroying it. Gideon perished in the resulting destruction. The death of Moff Gideon and the destruction of the Mandalore Imperial base marked the end of Gideon's Imperial remnant. ===Legacy=== {{Quote|There's no proof of any coordination between the scattered and dwindling number of Imperial forces.''"
"''What about the conflict on Mandalore?''"
"''Exactly my point. Gideon was a warlord acting on his own. There is no proof of a greater conspiracy and thus no immediate threat to this Republic.|Hamato Xiono and Carson Teva on Gideon's actions as a warning to the New Republic|}} Sometime after the [[conflict on Mandalore]], Carson Teva cited Gideon's battle as an example of how there had been coordination among the scattered and dwindling Imperial remnants during [[General]] [[Hera Syndulla]]'s admonishing session at [[Coruscant]] for disobeying the orders of the [[New Republic Senate]] to ignore the attempts of [[Morgan Elsbeth's forces]] to bring Grand Admiral Thrawn from [[Far galaxy|another galaxy]]. However, [[Senator]] [[Hamato Xiono]] dismissed Teva's intervention as not a proof that there was a greater conspiracy posing a threat immediately to the Republic, naively opining that Gideon had been a warlord acting on his own.{{Ahsoka|Part Seven: Dreams and Madness}} ==Behind the scenes== [[File:Gideon-Remnant-Concept.png|thumb|left|250px|Concept art of Moff Gideon and his Imperial remnant]] Gideon's Imperial remnant first appeared in "[[Chapter 1: The Mandalorian]]," the debut episode of [[Jon Favreau]]'s [[Disney+]] television series ''[[Star Wars: The Mandalorian]]'', which was directed by [[Dave Filoni]] and aired on [[November 12]], [[2019]].{{WebCite|url=https://lumiere-a.akamaihd.net/v1/documents/the_mandalorian_project_one-sheet_10_ec1e005f.pdf|text=The Mandalorian Media Kit|work=[https://dtcimedia.disney.com Disney Direct-to-Consumer & International]|archivedate=20230315011507}} For the episodes "[[Chapter 7: The Reckoning]]" and "[[Chapter 8: Redemption]]," Favreau and Filoni enlisted the help of the [[501st Legion (fan organization)|501st Legion]] fan organization as the crew of the series did not have enough stormtrooper costumes on set. organization.{{WebCite|url=https://www.cbr.com/the-mandalorian-501st-legion-stormtrooper-extras|text=The Mandalorian Enlisted the Help of Stormtrooper Group the 501st Legion|author=Noah
